A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. All pages were inspected, including v2's Appendix A; v1 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original DAVIS and Pexels experiments, quantitative baseline and ablation results in Table 1, and qualitative results in Figures 3–7.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds training-set-size and motion-conditioning experiments in Appendix A, Figure 7, and Table 2.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2 retain attention-map rotation, value/output projection fine-tuning, and dual-directional sampling with averaging and recurrence. Appendix A.3 adds implementation pseudocode without establishing an intentional redesign of the method.

E1.justification: Training remains based on SVD-generated videos, and evaluation retains DAVIS/Pexels distant-keyframe interpolation with the same described motion categories. Sample-count changes and parameter sweeps do not establish different coverage. The removed endpoint-variation example is a case study within the retained task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FILM, TRF, and DynamiCrafter. New Table 2 reuses FILM and TRF results as reference comparisons. Newly cited FLAVR and Video Frame Interpolation Transformer are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 expands Pexels evaluation from 45 to 106 input pairs, while DAVIS remains at 117. Appendix A introduces training-size settings of 50 and 150 videos around the existing 100, and motion bucket IDs 65 and 255 around the retained default 127. These substantially extend the evaluated settings.

E4.justification: Appendices A.1–A.2 add two sensitivity investigations: dependence on training-set size and on motion conditioning. The original component ablations and failure analysis remain. Conversely, v1's Section 5.5 and Figure 7 demonstration of varying the ending keyframe while fixing the starting frame are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new appendix continues reporting point estimates without error bars.

E6.justification: All Pexels entries in Table 1 change on the expanded evaluation sample; for example, the proposed method's FID/FVD changes from 34.58/366.53 to 22.99/306.84. These are replacement results under different sample counts, not demonstrated same-setting gains. DAVIS entries remain identical. New sensitivity results are added, and the adaptive-ending example is removed.

T1.justification: The diffusion and attention definitions, attention-rotation relation, and mathematical content of Algorithms 1–2 are retained. The appendix adds empirical analyses and implementation pseudocode, without new theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: lightweight backward-motion adaptation, consistent dual-directional sampling, and improved interpolation relative to existing methods. Explicitly naming the evaluation datasets does not change these claims' substantive scope.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 interprets the differing effects of motion bucket settings through endpoint constraints and differences between dataset motions. Section 6 additionally suggests better motion datasets and articulated/physical priors as possible remedies. Existing limitations concerning SVD motion priors, articulation, and sparse correspondences remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds training and sampling pseudocode, precise trainable-weight names, and classifier-free guidance branches; a footnote identifies the SVD-XT checkpoint. v2 also reports the under-2% trainable parameter share and removes the explicit project-page link. Documentation contains inconsistencies, including AdamW in the pseudocode versus Adam in Section 4.4.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds FLAVR (Kalluri et al., 2023) and Video Frame Interpolation Transformer (Shi et al., 2022), briefly extending discussion to direct CNN/transformer interpolation and multiple adjacent inputs. The broader positioning relative to diffusion interpolation and joint sampling remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section ordering remain closely matched. Changes include adding 'Diffusion' to the title, terminology cleanup, limited explanatory additions, author-year citations, removal of the adaptive-generation subsection, and organization of the new material into Appendix A.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column formatting to a single-column ICLR layout, resizing and relocating figures and algorithms throughout. Figure 4 gains an intermediate-frame column and red highlights. The original Figure 7 is removed; v2 adds a training-size plot, Table 2, and two pseudocode figures.

improvement.justification: The expanded Pexels evaluation and new training-size and motion-conditioning analyses provide more informative validation of the retained method. The net gain is limited by removal of the adaptive-ending demonstration and project link, plus errors in the new pseudocode, such as Figure 9 using pred_noise before initialization in its fusion expression.
